title: Book Income vs Taxable Income
description: Understand why financial accounting income and taxable income can differ.
html:
Two different systems

A company's income reported in its financial statements is not necessarily the same as its taxable income.

Book Income

Determined using financial accounting principles for financial reporting.

Taxable Income

Determined using applicable income tax laws and regulations.

Why can they differ?

Financial accounting rules and tax rules may recognize certain revenues or expenses differently.

Sometimes the difference is only about timing.

Other differences may never reverse.

Simple timing example

Assume financial reporting recognizes an expense of $10,000 this year.

Tax law does not allow the deduction until a future year.

Book income and taxable income can therefore differ this year even though the tax deduction may occur later.

Current income taxes

Taxable income is used in determining the company's current income tax obligation under the applicable tax law.

Foundation

Book Income ≠ Automatically Taxable Income

The important question is: Why are they different?

quiz.prompt: Why can financial statement income differ from taxable income?

choices.text: Because financial reporting and tax rules may recognize items differently
Because companies are never required to pay taxes
Because taxable income always equals cash flow
Because book income excludes all expenses

quiz.explanation: Financial reporting rules and tax rules can differ in the timing or treatment of revenues and expenses.
